basis: Focal neurologic dystonia directly disrupts laryngeal function; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Idiopathic inflammation and fibrosis of lung interstitium; infection or autoimmune disease is not required.
Inherited bile transport disorder causing recurrent hepatic cholestasis; pruritus and jaundice do not establish skin or eye damage.
Mycobacterial infection of lymph nodes; lymph node involvement alone does not establish blood or marrow disease.
Mitochondrial energy disorder; cardiomegaly 9/9, anemia 7/7 and hearing impairment 1/1 support involvement, though hearing evidence is limited.
Follicular skin atrophy, perioral pigmentation, milia and epidermoid cysts define a cutaneous disorder.
Chronic allergic inflammation directly affects cornea and conjunctiva; associated atopic dermatitis is a separate disease.
Inherited intestinal B12 malabsorption causes megaloblastic anemia; renal tubular protein reabsorption dysfunction produces proteinuria in about 50%.
Developmental narrowing of the coronary sinus, a cardiac venous structure.
Developmental impairment, hypertrichosis and gingival overgrowth define syndrome; optic nerve hypoplasia 2/3; skeletal anomalies in at least 1/3 omitted by cap.
Regional sensory and autonomic dysfunction defines CRPS1; edema, color changes and sweating do not establish additional organ damage.
Primary magnesium disturbance and obesity define metabolic involvement; generalized seizures and intellectual disability define neurologic involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental impairment and frequent seizures; feeding difficulty does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Carcinoma originates in the stomach; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Hereditary peripheral axonal neuropathy; optic atrophy with visual impairment occurs in 3/6 patients. Respiratory failure is very rare.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction defect; weakness does not establish primary muscle disease. Ocular findings lack a clear subtype-specific frequency.
Eczema 2/2; enteropathy with villous atrophy 1/2 and chronic diarrhea 2/2; pulmonary fibrosis 1/2; arthritis 1/2 omitted by cap.
Hereditary loss or scarcity of scalp and body hair; no additional organ disorder is established.
Androgen hormone resistance is an endocrine disorder; reproductive anomalies and reduced androgen-dependent hair do not establish additional organ damage.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and digital skeletal malformations define the syndrome; congenital absence of nails occurs in 7/7 patients.
Familial focal epilepsy arising from mesial temporal networks; hippocampal atrophy in a subgroup remains within the neurologic axis.
Generalized exfoliative dermatitis with immune dysfunction; chronic enteropathy with diarrhea and failure to thrive is defining and occurs in 80-99%.
Structural skeletal myopathy; ptosis 12/14 and ophthalmoparesis 3/4 impair ocular function. Neuropathy and respiratory insufficiency occur in only 5-29%.
Lysosomal storage causes progressive neurodegeneration; dysostosis multiplex 16/16 and hearing impairment in roughly half; hepatomegaly alone is not liver dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 16/16 patients; no extra-auditory disease is established.
